title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from pp. 59-68). A set E carries a symmetric 'orthogonality' or 'disjointness' relation x |o| y. It extends to subsets: A |o| B means every a in A is orthogonal to every b in B. From it one gets the polarity/Galois closure operators:
- cosupp°(A) = {y : y |o| A}, the orthocomplement;
- supp°(A) = cosupp°(cosupp°(A)), the closure.
Σ_E is the complete ortholattice of closed sets. A correspondence α : E → P(E') induces a union-preserving map ᾱ : P(E) → P(E'). α is 'compatible' if x |o| y implies ᾱ(x) |o| ᾱ(y). It induces α_* : Σ_E → Σ_E', A ↦ supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)).

The problem (p.62) is to make α_* commute with orthocomplementation, formula (**). Grothendieck introduces a reverse correspondence β : E' → P(E) satisfying (*): ᾱ(β(x')) ⊂ supp°({x'}). Given the needed fidelity, the argument yields β(x') |o| β(y'). By compatibility this gives ᾱβ(x') |o| ᾱβ(y'), the first line of this page. To conclude x' |o| y' one needs (*) to be an equality up to closure: supp°(ᾱ(β(x'))) = supp°({x'}).

He then proposes the optimal β, namely β = α* with α*(x') = {x ∈ E : α(x) ⊂ supp°({x'})}. This is the largest β satisfying (*); it is the residual/right-adjoint-type 'transpose' of α relative to the closure. With this choice (*) holds trivially. One then has to postulate:
(i) supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(α*(x'))) = supp°_{E'}({x'}) for all x'. This replaces the surjectivity hypothesis of the earlier example.
(ii) 'Faithful compatibility': x |o| y ⇔ ᾱ(x) |o| ᾱ(y).

On the next page he worries that (i) and (ii) are too strong, perhaps forcing α_* to be bijective. He writes that he does not yet understand the situation well. So the page is an exploratory step towards a good notion of morphism between orthogonality spaces that induces ortho-preserving maps of the closure lattices.
errors: No mathematical error. (i) is exactly what is needed: a set is orthogonal to x' iff it is orthogonal to supp°{x'}, so equal closures give x' |o| ᾱB ⇔ ᾱβ(x') |o| ᾱB. Pointwise (ii) is equivalent to its set version because ᾱ preserves unions and |o| on sets is defined pointwise.
The reference '(5)' in the transcription is presumably to the condition (*) of p.62.
The page sets hypotheses but does not prove that (i)+(ii) yield (**) in general. The author himself flags on p.68 that the hypotheses may be too strong.

ideas.what: Closure lattice Σ_E of a symmetric orthogonality relation (supp° = double orthocomplement, cosupp° = orthocomplement)
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space (Dacey space / orthoframe) and its complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets; Birkhoff polarity

ideas.what: Correspondences α : E → P(E') as morphisms, with induced union-preserving ᾱ and induced map α_* on closed sets; question of commutation with orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of orthogonality spaces / ortholattice homomorphisms induced by relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Paseka-Vetterlein (categories of orthogonality spaces, ~2020-22); earlier quantum-logic literature (Moore, Faure-Frölicher on projective geometries)

ideas.what: Optimal reverse correspondence α*(x') = {x : α(x) ⊂ supp°{x'}}, with the closure condition (i) and faithful compatibility (ii)
ideas.modern_name: Residuated / adjoint relation (Galois-connection transpose); adjointable maps between orthogonality spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Residuation theory (Blyth-Janowitz); adjointable maps between orthosets (Paseka-Vetterlein)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 notes develop a categorical treatment of orthogonality ('disposition') relations. Morphisms are correspondences equipped with a transpose α*, and conditions are sought under which the induced map on biorthogonally closed sets preserves orthocomplements. This closely anticipates the recent study of morphisms and adjointable maps between orthogonality spaces (orthosets) in quantum-logic research, which does not cite him.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only historical interest unless the surrounding pages contain a definitive theorem. On this page the thread is explicitly unfinished: he says on p.68 that he has not understood the situation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine Galois-connection/polarity manipulation, exploratory and self-acknowledged as unsatisfactory. Its main interest is that Grothendieck was working on morphisms of orthogonality structures in 1986, a little-known context.
